en: Pure, supreme, of the nature of existence, consciousness, and bliss, the substratum of qualities yet devoid of any substratum, most excellent,
great, radiant, within the cave [of the heart], and beyond all qualities.
I take refuge in Rāma, the ultimate bliss, the self-effulgent light. || 1 ||
Śiva, eternal, one, all-pervading, known as the Savior, whose form is bliss yet devoid of form, most venerable,
the Great Lord, the Lord of the Kalās, the Lord of the gods, the Supreme Lord.
I take refuge in the lord of men, the lord of the earth, who is himself without a superior lord. || 2 ||
That which Śiva described at the time of death into the root of Kārttikeya’s ear in Kāśī— “Rāma, Rāma, Rāma”—
that alone is the supreme form of the Tāraka-Brahman.
I worship, I worship, I worship, I worship. || 3 ||
Seated comfortably upon a beautiful great jewel-throne rooted in the Kalpa-tree, shining like ten million suns,
he is always accompanied by Jānakī and Lakṣmaṇa— this one [Lord].
I always worship Rāmacandra; I worship him. || 4 ||
His lotus-feet resound with jeweled anklets;
he is adorned with a shimmering girdle and beautiful yellow garments; his body is radiant with great jewel necklaces and the Kaustubha gem.
A garland trembling like a cluster of *cañcarī* flowers swaying in the wind.
Shining with the luster of the rising sun and moon, resembling the glow of lips as red as the moonlight of karma,
and [receiving] the crest-jewels of millions of bowing Brahmās, Rudras, and others—
Whose feet are worshipped by the lustration rite of shimmering splendor.
I worship, I worship Rāmacandra forever— him who, with his auspicious seal of consciousness, awakens his devotees such as Añjaneya and others standing before him with palms joined in reverence.
I do not think of anyone other than you; I do not think of anyone other than you; I do not think of anyone other than you. || 7 ||
When Kṛtānta approaches me and attempts to terrify me with his soldiers of fierce majesty,
then you shall manifest your true form.
Then, [he beheld] the destruction of calamities, together with bow and arrow. || 8 ||
Be present within the temple of my mind; be gracious, be gracious, O Lord Rāmacandra,
together with the son of Kaikeyī and Saumitri.
Being served according to one's own capacity and with devotion.
O Rāma, be gracious with your many armies led by monkey lords and earthly kings who are foremost among your devotees;
salutations to you, salutations be to you, O Lord Rāma, be gracious!
Command me, command me clearly, O Lord! || 10 ||
You alone are my supreme destiny, for you are that one, pure consciousness; I consider nothing other than you to exist,
since from you arose the immeasurable ether, air, and fire.
The effects, such as water and earth, are both moving and unmoving.
Salutations to You, Rāma, the God of gods, whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss; salutations to You,
the Lord of Jānakī’s life.
Salutations to you, whose eyes are as long as lotus petals. || 12 ||
Salutations to you who are devotedly loved by those possessed of bhakti; salutations to you who can be attained solely through a mass of merit;
salutations to the primordial Person, who is known through the Vedas.
Salutations to the Beautiful One, the beloved of Indirā. || 13 ||
Homage to the creator of the universe, homage to the destroyer of the universe,
homage to the enjoyer of the universe, homage to the mother of the universe;
homage to the eye of the universe, homage to the conqueror of the universe.
Homage to the father of the universe; homage to the mother of the universe. || 14 ||
O Rāma, even a stone, through the grace of the dust from the contact with the earth of your feet, indeed attains consciousness;
how much more so a human being by performing service to your two feet!
That this very consciousness is [the self]—what is there to wonder at today? || 15 ||
O Rāmacandra, those men who daily remember your wondrous and purifying conduct— worshipping you,
the ender of worldly existence, while sustaining their own being;
They obtain their end, yet they do not perceive it until the very conclusion.
He is meritorious, he is worthy of honor, and he is my refuge—
this man who knows you, the crest-jewel of the gods,
the one whose form is eternal, whose nature is consciousness and bliss.
O Rāma, that supreme state is beyond the reach of mind and speech.
O Lord Rāmacandra, whose abundant heroic enemies have been overwhelmed by the power of your fierce majesty,
how can your strength be described when you were yet in extreme childhood?
For by him was shattered the staff-like bow of Caṇḍīśa. || 18 ||
O Rāma, what hero or man, other than you, could [conquer] the fierce Ten-necked one, together with his sons, his friends, and the hosts of Rākṣasas stationed within the mountain fastnesses?
"Whether a god or an immortal, who could conquer [him] in the three worlds? || 19 ||

I bow to him who always drinks the nectar of Rāma, saying "Rāma, Rāma"— that nectar which is the root of the flow of bliss and the source of constant delight— and who, with beautiful teeth, laughs while bowing down.
I worship that Hanumān most intensely from within.
O Death, by drinking daily and constantly the nectar of Rāma— namely "Rāma, Rāma"— which is the root of the flow of bliss and where Rāma is ever present, I am indeed not subject to death.
I fear neither prosperity nor adversity, for they depend solely upon your grace.
[The earth was] adorned by those who were not black (fair-complexioned), who were not joined with Sītā (not married to Sītā), whose bows were not on the ground (who held their bows),

who were not enemies of Rāma (allies of Rāma), who were not to be saluted by Saumitri (not inferior to Lakṣmaṇa), whose majesty was not fierce (gentle in power), who were not lords of Laṅkā (not kings of Laṅkā), and who were not friends of Sugrīva (not allies of Sugrīva).
Enough with these deities whose designations are merely conventional! || 22 ||
By those seated in the *avīrāsana* posture, adorned with the *acinmudrā*,
who illuminate the reality of the non-devotee, Hanumān, and others, and who possess abundant *mandāra* roots and abundant *mandāra* garlands;
Enough with these deities whose names we have already heard! || 23 ||
With the fury of no ocean, with majesty beyond praise, with expeditions requiring no kinsmen, enriched by gentle smiles,
with exiles requiring no punishment, and with unimpeded awakening—
Enough with these deities who are subject to decay; let them not concern us. || 24 ||
"O Hare Rāma! O Lord of Sītā! O Enemy of Rāvaṇa! O Enemy of Khara! O Murāri! O Enemy of the Asuras!
O Pāra!"—thus he was constantly speaking and leading [the way].
O friend of all, look upon me with your gaze! 25 ||
Salutations to you, O son of Sumitrā, who are worthy of worship; salutations to you, O delighter of Kaikeyī, who are always to be praised;
salutations to you, O lord of monkeys, who are eternally honored.
Salutations to you, salutations to you, O Rāmacandra, forever! || 26 ||
Be gracious, be gracious, O you of fierce majesty!
Be gracious, be gracious, O Destroyer of the fierce enemy!
Be gracious, be gracious, O you who have compassion for those who seek refuge!
Be gracious, be gracious, O Lord Rāmacandra! || 27 ||
Thus ends the *Śrīrāmabhujaṅgaprayātastotra*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
Om! May this be an offering unto the Supreme Brahman, Śrī Rāmacandra, accompanied by Śrī Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa, Bharata, Śatrughna, and Hanumān.
